claim: Direct electron detectors have higher detective quantum efficiency than photographic film.
source: The recent introduction of direct electron detection cameras with much better detective quantum efficiency (DQE) has meant that images having higher SNR can be obtained with the same, or lower, total electron exposure.
evidence: Stated as a known fact about direct electron detectors compared to previous technology

claim: Direct electron detectors have frame rates that make it possible to collect videos of particles during an exposure.
source: In addition, these cameras have frame rates which make it possible to collect videos of the particles in the thin film of vitreous water during an exposure, and thus partially correct for the effects of beam-induced particle movement and specimen drift.
evidence: Stated as a known capability of direct electron detectors

claim: Electron irradiation causes random translations and rotations of particles, which are typically largest in the first few frames.
source: Using a 70-MDa virus that can be accurately aligned even at short exposures, it was shown that electron irradiation causes random translations and rotations of the particles, which are typically largest in the first few frames (Brilot et al., 2012; Campbell et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: A 3.3 Å resolution map of the D7 proteasome was produced from 126,000 particles.
source: Both studies produced maps of unprecedented resolution, 3.3 Å for the D7 proteasome from 126,000 particles and 4.5 Å from 35,000 asymmetric 80S ribosomes.
evidence: Cited as a result from previous studies

claim: A 4.5 Å resolution map of the 80S ribosome was produced from 35,000 asymmetric units.
source: Both studies produced maps of unprecedented resolution, 3.3 Å for the D7 proteasome from 126,000 particles and 4.5 Å from 35,000 asymmetric 80S ribosomes.
evidence: Cited as a result from previous studies

claim: Frh is a 1.2 MDa complex.
source: Recently we determined the structure of the 1.2 MDa Frh complex, the F420-dependent hydrogenase from Methanothermobacter marburgensis, ab initio from cryo-EM data collected on photographic film (Mills et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a known property of the Frh complex

claim: Frh is a key enzyme in the metabolism of methanogenic archaea.
source: Frh is a key enzyme in the metabolism of methanogenic archaea, where the reduction of carbon dioxide to methane involves the oxidation of four molecules of H2 by a number of different hydrogenases.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about Frh function

claim: The reduced form of the F420 coenzyme is regenerated by Frh.
source: The reduced form of the F420 coenzyme, which is the electron donor in several of these steps, is regenerated by Frh (Thauer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Frh comprises approximately 2% of the soluble cell protein in methanogens.
source: The central role of Frh in the metabolism of methanogens is reflected in its abundance (∼2%) in the soluble cell protein (Fox et al., 1987).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Frh is a heterotrimeric enzyme composed of FrhA (43 kDa), FrhG (26 kDa), and FrhB (31 kDa).
source: Frh is a heterotrimeric enzyme composed of the 43 kDa subunit FrhA that contains a [NiFe]-center, the 26 kDa subunit FrhG with three [4Fe4S] clusters, and the 31 kDa iron–sulphur flavoprotein FrhB, which contains the F420-binding site and has one [4Fe4S] cluster and an FAD.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about Frh structure

claim: FrhA contains a [NiFe]-center.
source: Frh is a heterotrimeric enzyme composed of the 43 kDa subunit FrhA that contains a [NiFe]-center, the 26 kDa subunit FrhG with three [4Fe4S] clusters, and the 31 kDa iron–sulphur flavoprotein FrhB, which contains the F420-binding site and has one [4Fe4S] cluster and an FAD.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about FrhA composition

claim: FrhG contains three [4Fe4S] clusters.
source: Frh is a heterotrimeric enzyme composed of the 43 kDa subunit FrhA that contains a [NiFe]-center, the 26 kDa subunit FrhG with three [4Fe4S] clusters, and the 31 kDa iron–sulphur flavoprotein FrhB, which contains the F420-binding site and has one [4Fe4S] cluster and an FAD.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about FrhG composition

claim: FrhB contains the F420-binding site.
source: Frh is a heterotrimeric enzyme composed of the 43 kDa subunit FrhA that contains a [NiFe]-center, the 26 kDa subunit FrhG with three [4Fe4S] clusters, and the 31 kDa iron–sulphur flavoprotein FrhB, which contains the F420-binding site and has one [4Fe4S] cluster and an FAD.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about FrhB function

claim: FrhB contains one [4Fe4S] cluster and an FAD.
source: Frh is a heterotrimeric enzyme composed of the 43 kDa subunit FrhA that contains a [NiFe]-center, the 26 kDa subunit FrhG with three [4Fe4S] clusters, and the 31 kDa iron–sulphur flavoprotein FrhB, which contains the F420-binding site and has one [4Fe4S] cluster and an FAD.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about FrhB composition

claim: The Frh complex is a dodecamer with tetrahedral symmetry.
source: Our cryo-EM study showed that the Frh complex is a dodecamer with tetrahedral symmetry.
evidence: Stated as a finding from previous cryo-EM study by the authors

claim: A previous cryo-EM map of Frh from film data had approximately 5 Å resolution.
source: The map had ∼5 Å resolution which was sufficient to show secondary structure and density for many side chains as well as the cofactors forming the electron transfer chain, making it possible to trace the three protein chains, one of them without a template.
evidence: Stated as a result from the authors' previous study

claim: A new cryo-EM map of Frh was reconstructed from 26,000 particles at 3.36 Å resolution.
source: The resulting map from 26,000 particles has a resolution of 3.36 Å, which enabled us to refine the model obtained from film data.
evidence: Stated as a result from the current study

claim: Images were collected using the FEI Falcon-II detector in video mode with 18 frames per second.
source: Images of the Frh complex were collected using the back-thinned FEI Falcon-II in video mode with 18 frames per second.
evidence: Stated as a method used in the current study

claim: A dataset of 33,590 particles (403,080 asymmetric units) was collected from 235 images.
source: A dataset of 33,590 particles (403,080 asymmetric units) at a defocus range of 0.8–3.5 µm was collected from 235 images in two sessions on a single grid.
evidence: Stated as data collection results

claim: The defocus range used was 0.8–3.5 µm.
source: A dataset of 33,590 particles (403,080 asymmetric units) at a defocus range of 0.8–3.5 µm was collected from 235 images in two sessions on a single grid.
evidence: Stated as a parameter of data collection

claim: The Frh complex has a diameter of approximately 175 Å.
source: Areas of very thin ice were selected that we estimate to be only slightly thicker than the particle diameter of ∼175 Å
evidence: Stated as an estimate based on observations

claim: A first refinement using the sum of the first 20 video frames yielded a map at 3.94 Å resolution.
source: A first refinement using the sum of the first 20 video frames (discarding the last 4 frames because of likely radiation damage [Baker and Rubinstein, 2010]) yielded a map at 3.94 Å resolution (Figure 2A)
evidence: Stated as a result from data processing, shown in Figure 2A

claim: The first frame of videos showed a large movement in comparison with subsequent frames in the majority of cases.
source: In the majority of cases, the first frame showed a large movement in comparison with the others (Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated as an observation from frame alignment analysis, shown in Figure 3A

claim: Discarding the first frame results in a higher-resolution map than including it.
source: We refined the sum of the aligned frames with or without the first frame and found that discarding the first frame results in a higher-resolution map (Figure 3B).
evidence: Stated as a result from comparative refinement, shown in Figure 3B

claim: Refinement of 20 aligned frames resulted in a 3.74 Å map.
source: The refinement of the 20 aligned frames resulted in a 3.74 Å map (Figure 2A).
evidence: Stated as a result from data processing, shown in Figure 2A

claim: Statistical alignment procedure using a running average of 5 frames gave the best resolution among particle-based methods.
source: This procedure also improved the resolution relative to the unaligned particles in a very similar way to the whole-frame alignment (Figure 2A); the best resolution was obtained when 5 frames were averaged.
evidence: Stated as a result from testing different frame averaging parameters, shown in Figure 2A

claim: Combining whole-frame and particle-based alignment procedures resulted in a 3.69 Å resolution map.
source: In yet another approach we combined the two alignment procedures (whole-frame and particle-based). The resolution curve of this refinement gave a better FSC than the others over all frequencies and the resulting reconstruction had a resolution of 3.69 Å (Figure 2A)
evidence: Stated as a result from combined alignment approach, shown in Figure 2A

claim: For the intermediate-sized Frh particle, the combination of whole-frame and particle-based alignment procedures works best.
source: indicating that for the intermediate-sized particle investigated here the combination of the two alignment procedures works best.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from comparing different alignment methods

claim: Reducing the number of averaged frames to 6 gave the best resolution of 3.39 Å.
source: Every omitted frame improved the map resolution until only 6 frames were averaged. This gave the best resolution of 3.39 Å, compared to 3.74 Å for all 20 frames (Figure 2B).
evidence: Stated as a result from testing different numbers of frames, shown in Figure 2B

claim: Reducing the number of averaged frames to fewer than 6 made the resolution worse.
source: Reducing the number of averaged frames further to 4 or 5 made the resolution worse.
evidence: Stated as a result from testing fewer frames

claim: Adding 15,000 particles from a third microscope session reduced the map resolution.
source: A third microscope session on a different grid yielded another 15,000 particles. Adding them, however, reduced the map resolution and these images were therefore not included in further steps.
evidence: Stated as a result from attempting to add more data

claim: The third dataset had worse data quality because of thicker ice on the grid.
source: We assume the data quality was worse because of the thicker ice on this grid, which had made it necessary to use a higher defocus, never less than 1.2 µm, to distinguish the particles.
evidence: Stated as an inference about why the third dataset was of lower quality

claim: Removing images with high defocus (>2.5 µm) and poor quality reduced the dataset from 33,590 to 26,635 particles.
source: We removed the images with high defocus (>2.5 µm) and those that were of poor quality as judged by the visibility and symmetry of the Thon rings. This reduced the dataset by 20% from 33,590 to 26,635 particles (319,620 asymmetric units).
evidence: Stated as a data processing step and its result

claim: Refinement of the reduced dataset with 6 frames averaged resulted in a 3.36 Å resolution map.
source: Refinement of this smaller dataset under otherwise identical conditions resulted in maps with better resolution than the full dataset, and the best map, with 6 frames averaged, extended to 3.36 Å resolution (Figures 2C and 4).
evidence: Stated as the final result from optimized data processing, shown in Figures 2C and 4

claim: The accumulated dose for the final 6-frame data was approximately 24 e−/Å2.
source: The accumulated dose for this data was ∼24 e−/Å2.
evidence: Stated as a calculated parameter of the final dataset

claim: The local resolution map was featureless, indicating that the dodecameric Frh complex is completely rigid.
source: We tested the local resolution of the map with the program ResMap (Kucukelbir et al., 2014) to identify possible flexible protein regions. The local resolution map was featureless (not shown), indicating that the dodecameric Frh complex is completely rigid.
evidence: Stated as a result from local resolution analysis and its interpretation

claim: A map from the last 6 frames (pre-irradiated with ~24 e−/Å2) had 3.94 Å resolution.
source: we also created maps of the last 6 and the middle 6 frames of the 20-frame videos of the reduced dataset, averaging particles that were in effect pre-irradiated with ∼24 and 49 e−/Å2. This resulted in maps of 3.94 and 4.16 Å resolution, respectively
evidence: Stated as a result from analyzing radiation damage effects

claim: A map from the middle 6 frames (pre-irradiated with ~49 e−/Å2) had 4.16 Å resolution.
source: we also created maps of the last 6 and the middle 6 frames of the 20-frame videos of the reduced dataset, averaging particles that were in effect pre-irradiated with ∼24 and 49 e−/Å2. This resulted in maps of 3.94 and 4.16 Å resolution, respectively
evidence: Stated as a result from analyzing radiation damage effects

claim: Pre-irradiation resulted in poorer visibility of side chain densities.
source: which was clearly reflected in the poorer visibility of side chain densities (Figure 5).
evidence: Stated as an observation from comparing maps with different pre-irradiation doses, shown in Figure 5

claim: The 3.36 Å map shows all secondary structure clearly.
source: The reconstructed density map shows all secondary structure as well as clear side chain densities for most residues.
evidence: Stated as a description of the final map quality

claim: The 3.36 Å map shows clear side chain densities for most residues.
source: The reconstructed density map shows all secondary structure as well as clear side chain densities for most residues.
evidence: Stated as a description of the final map quality

claim: The full coordination of all cofactors in the electron transfer chain is clearly visible in the 3.36 Å map.
source: The full coordination of all cofactors in the electron transfer chain (a [NiFe] center, four [4Fe4S] clusters and an FAD) is clearly visible along with a well-defined substrate access channel.
evidence: Stated as a description of the final map quality

claim: A well-defined substrate access channel is visible in the 3.36 Å map.
source: The full coordination of all cofactors in the electron transfer chain (a [NiFe] center, four [4Fe4S] clusters and an FAD) is clearly visible along with a well-defined substrate access channel.
evidence: Stated as a description of the final map quality

claim: Catalysis by Frh is diffusion-limited and does not depend on protein flexibility or conformational changes.
source: From the rigidity of the complex we conclude that catalysis is diffusion-limited and does not depend on protein flexibility or conformational changes.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion drawn from the observed rigidity of the complex

claim: Alpha helices and beta sheets were easily recognizable in the 3.36 Å map.
source: Alpha helices (Figure 7) and beta sheets (Figure 8) were easily recognizable
evidence: Stated as an observation about map quality, shown in Figures 7 and 8

claim: The large majority of side chains had good density in the 3.36 Å map.
source: and the large majority of side chains had good density (Figure 9; Video 2).
evidence: Stated as an observation about map quality, shown in Figure 9 and Video 2

claim: Most of the protein could be fitted to the map using real space refinement in Coot.
source: Most of the protein could be fitted to the map using the 'real space refine' feature in Coot, which had not been possible for the lower resolution map from film images.
evidence: Stated as a result of model building

claim: The FSC between the final map and a map calculated from the fitted model is 0.5 at 3.56 Å resolution.
source: The FSC between this map and a map calculated from the fitted model is 0.5 at 3.56 Å resolution, close to the resolution of the final map, confirming the correctness of the fit (Figure 10).
evidence: Stated as a validation result, shown in Figure 10

claim: All three subunits were traced completely except for a few N- or C-terminal residues, accounting for 893 out of 903 amino acids.
source: All three subunits were traced completely except for a few N- or C-terminal residues, accounting for 893 out of 903 amino acids (Figure 11).
evidence: Stated as a result of model building, shown in Figure 11

claim: All three proteins had been traced essentially correctly in the lower-resolution film map.
source: We found that all three proteins had been traced essentially correctly in the lower-resolution film map (Video 3).
evidence: Stated as a comparison between the new and old models, shown in Video 3

claim: The largest differences between the two models were found in surface loops that had been difficult to trace in the film map.
source: The largest differences between the two models were found in surface loops that had been difficult to trace in the film map.
evidence: Stated as a comparison between the new and old models

claim: A 12-residue stretch in FrhG (188–199) that was unresolved in the previous model is now resolved as two alpha-helices (194–201 and 208–215).
source: The only unresolved part in the previous model involved a 12-residue stretch in FrhG (188–199), for which no density was found and which was thought to form a flexible surface loop. In the new map, two nearby density features, modelled as extended loops before, were clearly recognizable as alpha-helices (194–201 and 208–215) that accommodate the missing residues.
evidence: Stated as a comparison between the new and old models

claim: The conserved cysteines C206 and C208 in FrhG are near a strong density on the dimer axis between two FrhG subunits.
source: The resulting shift of residues brings the cysteine residues C206 and C208, which are conserved in the FrhG family (Figure 11B), near a strong density on the dimer axis between two FrhG subunits.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the new model, shown in Figure 11B

claim: The density between four cysteine side chains (C206 and C208 from two FrhG subunits) is strongly suggestive of a coordinated ion.
source: The cysteines of the dimer partner are just a few Å away, and the density in between the four cysteine side chains is strongly suggestive of a coordinated ion (Figure 12).
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the density, shown in Figure 12

claim: The tetrahedral arrangement of the four cysteines suggests the coordinated ion is zinc.
source: Although the cysteine side chains are not completely resolved, their tetrahedral arrangement suggests that it is a zinc ion (Dokmanić et al., 2008; Harding et al., 2010; Rulíšek and Vondrášek, 1998; Zheng et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated as an inference based on structural arrangement and supported by citations

claim: The FAD cofactor in FrhB has continuous density in the map.
source: The FAD cofactor in FrhB has continuous density in the map, and its folded conformation with the adenine and isoalloxazine moieties in close proximity (Mills et al., 2013) is confirmed (Figure 13; Video 4).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figure 13 and Video 4

claim: The FAD has a folded conformation with the adenine and isoalloxazine moieties in close proximity.
source: The FAD cofactor in FrhB has continuous density in the map, and its folded conformation with the adenine and isoalloxazine moieties in close proximity (Mills et al., 2013) is confirmed (Figure 13; Video 4).
evidence: Stated as a confirmation of previous observation, shown in Figure 13 and Video 4

claim: The FAD is completely surrounded by conserved residues.
source: As noted before (Mills et al., 2013), the FAD is completely surrounded by conserved residues, including loops 23–30, 71–77, and 131–138 (which includes Cys134, a ligand of the nearby FeS cluster i.e., the electron donor to FAD) (Figure 11C).
evidence: Stated as an observation confirmed from previous study, shown in Figure 11C

claim: There is no density for the substrate F420 in the map.
source: There is no density for the substrate, F420, but the FAD is accessible from the surface through a ∼5 Å gap between the main body of FrhB and a domain formed by residues 128–188 containing an alpha helix and a three-stranded beta sheet (Video 5).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Video 5

claim: The FAD is accessible from the surface through a ~5 Å gap.
source: There is no density for the substrate, F420, but the FAD is accessible from the surface through a ∼5 Å gap between the main body of FrhB and a domain formed by residues 128–188 containing an alpha helix and a three-stranded beta sheet (Video 5).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Video 5

claim: The putative substrate access channel is completely lined by conserved residues.
source: This putative substrate access channel is, like the FAD itself, completely lined by conserved residues (Video 6).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Video 6

claim: The Falcon II data quality is far superior to that obtained with photographic film.
source: The Falcon II data quality is far superior to that obtained with photographic film.
evidence: Stated as a comparison between the two detection methods

claim: With film, a 5 Å map was obtained from 84,000 Frh particles.
source: With film we obtained a 5 Å map from 84,000 Frh particles (Mills et al., 2013)
evidence: Stated as a result from previous study

claim: With Falcon II, a map with better than 4 Å resolution was achieved from 70% fewer particles than with film.
source: but with Falcon II images of the same sample and the same electron microscope we were able to achieve a map with better than 4 Å resolution from 70% fewer particles.
evidence: Stated as a comparison of results between film and Falcon II

claim: The higher DQE of the Falcon II detector makes it possible to reliably detect particles at very low defocus.
source: The higher DQE of the detector makes it possible to reliably detect particles at very low defocus.
evidence: Stated as an advantage of the Falcon II detector

claim: With Falcon II, particles were clearly visible at 900 nm defocus, whereas with film particles could not be detected at less than 1500 nm defocus.
source: This is illustrated by Figure 1A, showing a micrograph taken at 900 nm defocus in which the particles are clearly visible, whereas with film we were not able to detect the particles at less than 1500 nm defocus.
evidence: Stated as a comparison between film and Falcon II, shown in Figure 1A

claim: The high-resolution signal for low-defocus images is very much better than that for images recorded at higher defocus.
source: The high-resolution signal for the low-defocus images is very much better than that for images recorded at higher defocus, which was a critical factor in attaining the final map.
evidence: Stated as an observation about data quality

claim: Both whole-frame and particle-based video alignment methods gave similar improvements in final map resolution compared to unaligned frames for the 1.2 MDa Frh complex.
source: For this complex we found that both video alignment methods gave similar improvements in final map resolution compared to unaligned frames (Figure 2A).
evidence: Stated as a result from comparing alignment methods, shown in Figure 2A

claim: The accumulated dose used for the 3.36 Å Frh map (~24 e/Å2) is very similar to the accumulated dose used for the 3.3 Å proteasome map (~21 e/Å2).
source: The accumulated dose in these frames was ∼24 e/Å2, very similar to the accumulated dose (∼21 e/Å2) used for the 3.3 Å proteasome map (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with previous study

claim: A 4.16 Å reconstruction from the last 6 frames still showed partial side chains and clear helices.
source: A 4.16 Å reconstruction after a refinement of only the last 6 frames of the 20-frame videos still showed partial side chains and clear helices (Figure 5C).
evidence: Stated as an observation about map quality despite radiation damage, shown in Figure 5C

claim: For smaller particles than the 1.2 MDa Frh complex, it would be advantageous to record videos over longer periods with higher cumulative doses.
source: In case of smaller particles than the 1.2 MDa Frh complex, it would be advantageous to record videos over longer periods with higher cumulative doses, so that the particles are more visible and easier to align.
evidence: Stated as a recommendation based on the current study

claim: Direct electron detectors provide a way to optimize a posteriori the electron exposure of the data used for reconstruction.
source: Thus, direct electron detectors provide a way to optimize a posteriori the electron exposure of the data used for reconstruction.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the advantages of direct electron detectors

claim: Side chains on the surface are in general not seen in the 3.36 Å map, probably due to their flexibility in the aqueous solvent.
source: Side chains on the surface are in general not seen, probably due to their flexibility in the aqueous solvent.
evidence: Stated as an observation and interpretation

claim: The side chains of glutamates and aspartates are almost all absent in the 3.36 Å map.
source: The only conspicuous exceptions are the side chains of glutamates and aspartates, which are almost all absent (Figure 9)
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figure 9

claim: An absence of aspartate and glutamate side chain densities can be observed in other high-resolution cryo-EM maps.
source: An absence of aspartate and glutamate side chain densities can also be observed in other high-resolution cryo-EM maps, including the electron crystallography maps of LHC-II (Kühlbrandt et al., 1994) and bacteriorhodopsin (Kimura et al., 1997) and the recent 3.3-Å single particle map of the 20S proteasome (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to other studies

claim: In X-ray crystallography, carboxylate side chains have higher B-factors after extended exposure to intense synchrotron radiation, possibly due to decarboxylation.
source: In X-ray crystallography it was noted that carboxylate side chains have higher B-factors after extended exposure to intense synchrotron radiation, possibly due to decarboxylation (Weik et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Synchrotron radiation damage on carboxylate side chains occurs at radiation doses equivalent to less than 1 e/Å2.
source: A quantification of synchrotron radiation damage on carboxylate side chains (Fioravanti et al., 2006) shows that this damage already occurs at radiation doses equivalent to less than 1 e/Å2 (Henderson, 1990), a much lower dose than is feasible in cryo-EM.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: Decarboxylation of aspartate and glutamate would have occurred well within the first frame of the video dataset.
source: This implies that the decarboxylation would have occurred well within the first frame of our video data set and aspartate and glutamate side chains would in general not be visible in cryo-EM maps.
evidence: Stated as an inference from radiation damage data

claim: FrhG Asp60 is involved in the coordination of the proximal FeS cluster and has visible density.
source: Among the few visible carboxylate side chains in Frh, two are involved in ligand binding: FrhG Asp60 in the coordination of the proximal FeS cluster, and FrhA Glu44 in liganding a possible Fe or Mg ion (Mills et al., 2013; Figure 15).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figure 15

claim: FrhA Glu44 is involved in liganding a possible Fe or Mg ion and has visible density.
source: Among the few visible carboxylate side chains in Frh, two are involved in ligand binding: FrhG Asp60 in the coordination of the proximal FeS cluster, and FrhA Glu44 in liganding a possible Fe or Mg ion (Mills et al., 2013; Figure 15).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figure 15

claim: In X-ray crystallography, not all glutamate and aspartate side chains are equally susceptible to radiation damage.
source: In X-ray crystallography it is also found that not all glutamate and aspartate side chains are equally susceptible to radiation damage, but the dependence on the structural and chemical environment is not well understood (Fioravanti et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: In the 3-Å bacteriorhodopsin EM map, the side chains of deprotonated Asp85 and Asp212 were invisible, whereas the protonated side chains of Asp96 and Asp115 had good density.
source: In the 3-Å bacteriorhodopsin EM map, the side chains of Asp85 and Asp212, which from spectroscopy are known to be deprotonated, were invisible, whereas the protonated side chains of Asp96 and Asp115 had good density (Kimura et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The structure of Frh was traced ab initio in the previous cryo-EM map from film data.
source: The structure of Frh was traced ab initio in our previous cryo-EM map from film data, which had a nominal overall resolution of 5.5 Å as determined by gold-standard FSC, but a significantly higher resolution of ∼4.5 Å in well-defined regions of the map (Mills et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a description of previous work

claim: The previous Frh structure from film data was essentially correct.
source: There were many indications that our original Frh structure was essentially correct, for example well-resolved hydrophobic side chains in the protein interior and the observation of secondary structure in regions where it was expected from prediction programs.
evidence: Stated as a validation of previous work

claim: It would hardly be possible to trace an electron density map obtained by X-ray crystallography at a nominal resolution of 5.5 Å.
source: Note that it would hardly be possible to trace an electron density map obtained by X-ray crystallography at a nominal resolution of 5.5 Å.
evidence: Stated as a comparison between cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography

claim: The difference in traceability between cryo-EM and X-ray maps at similar resolution reflects the quality of the phase information.
source: This clear difference reflects the quality of the phase information, which is conserved in the phase contrast electron micrographs and determined directly by image processing, whereas in X-ray crystallography it is determined indirectly by isomorphous replacement or anomalous scattering.
evidence: Stated as an explanation for the difference between cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography

claim: The function of Frh is the hydrogenation of F420 by molecular hydrogen.
source: Although the overall chain trace is the same, in detail the model based on the 3.36 Å map is of course much improved. The function of Frh is the hydrogenation of F420 by molecular hydrogen.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about Frh function

claim: Electrons are extracted from hydrogen by the [NiFe] cluster in FrhA and transferred via the three [4Fe4S] clusters in FrhG and another one in FrhB to FAD and from there to the substrate.
source: Electrons are extracted from hydrogen by the [NiFe] cluster in FrhA, and transferred via the three [4Fe4S] clusters in FrhG and another one in FrhB to FAD and from there to the substrate.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about the electron transfer pathway

claim: The electron transfer chain is clearly recognizable in the 3.36 Å map.
source: The electron transfer chain is clearly recognizable.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map

claim: The [NiFe] cluster has a high density and is coordinated by conserved residues.
source: The [NiFe] cluster has a high density (Figure 15B) and is coordinated by conserved residues, as in the large subunits of other [NiFe] hydrogenases (Figure 11A).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figures 15B and 11A

claim: There is another conserved ion near the [NiFe] cluster, coordinated among others by the C-terminal histidine of FrhA, His386.
source: Nearby is another ion, also conserved, coordinated among others by the C-terminal histidine of FrhA, His386 (Figure 15B).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figure 15B

claim: The four FeS clusters are arranged in a chain with distances of ~10 Å.
source: The four FeS clusters were easily localized in the film map because of their high density; moreover, they are arranged in a chain with distances of ∼10 Å (Mills et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a result from previous study

claim: In the Falcon II map, the tetrahedral coordination of the FeS clusters can be clearly seen.
source: In the Falcon II map, the clusters are not just featureless blobs, but their tetrahedral coordination (mostly by cysteine residues, or, in one case, an aspartate) can be clearly seen (Figure 6, Figure 15A).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map, shown in Figures 6 and 15A

claim: The orientation of the FeS clusters can be modelled correctly, with the irons facing the sulphurs of the cysteine side chains.
source: Thus their orientation can be modelled correctly, with the irons facing the sulphurs of the cysteine side chains.
evidence: Stated as a result of improved map quality

claim: The density for an ion on the dimer interface between two FrhG subunits was visible in the film map but not recognized as an ion.
source: One unexpected feature found in the new map was the density for an ion on the dimer interface between two FrhG subunits (Figure 12). This density feature was actually visible in the film map, but since the flanking conserved cysteines from the two FrhG subunits were not recognized, its interpretation as an ion was not obvious.
evidence: Stated as a comparison between the new and old maps, shown in Figure 12

claim: The function of the ion on the FrhG dimer interface is most likely to stabilize the dodecameric complex.
source: The function of this ion is most likely to stabilize the dodecameric complex, but its location between the two medial FeS clusters at a distance of only 9 Å, which is less than the distance of ∼10 Å between adjacent FeS clusters in the electron transfer chains, means that a role in electron transfer cannot be ruled out.
evidence: Stated as an inference about the ion's function

claim: A role in electron transfer for the ion on the FrhG dimer interface cannot be ruled out.
source: The function of this ion is most likely to stabilize the dodecameric complex, but its location between the two medial FeS clusters at a distance of only 9 Å, which is less than the distance of ∼10 Å between adjacent FeS clusters in the electron transfer chains, means that a role in electron transfer cannot be ruled out.
evidence: Stated as a speculation about the ion's function

claim: FAD acts as a one-electron/two-electron redox switch between the FeS clusters and the F420 substrate.
source: FAD acts as a one-electron/two-electron redox switch between the FeS clusters and the F420 substrate (Fox et al., 1987; Alex et al., 1990; Thauer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work

claim: The substrate needs to approach the FAD to within van der Waals distance to enable hydride transfer.
source: This means that the substrate needs to approach the FAD to within van der Waals distance to enable hydride transfer (Ceh et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: In a previous study, a density near the FAD isoalloxazine ring was interpreted as part of F420 at low occupancy.
source: In our previous study, we collected data from Frh with and without the substrate. In the map obtained in the presence of substrate we had identified a density near the FAD isoalloxazine ring that we interpreted as part of F420 at low occupancy (Mills et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a description of previous work

claim: The F420 binding pocket is clearly empty in the new Falcon-II map despite using a sample with a large excess of F420.
source: For the new Falcon-II map, we used an Frh sample with a large excess of F420, but the F420 binding pocket is clearly empty.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the new map

claim: The density interpreted as F420 in the film map must have been due to noise.
source: As the same sample was used in both studies, we conclude that the density in the film map must have been due to noise.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from comparing the two maps

claim: There is no indication of even a low occupancy of substrate or of flexibility in the F420 binding region.
source: There is no indication of even a low occupancy of substrate or of flexibility in this map region.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the map

claim: The protein region around the F420 binding pocket is rigid.
source: A map of local resolution (Kucukelbir et al., 2014) confirmed that the protein region around this pocket is rigid.
evidence: Stated as a result from local resolution analysis

claim: Conformational changes do not play a role for the access of F420 to the hydride donor.
source: This suggests that conformational changes do not play a role for the access of F420 to the hydride donor, consistent with the finding that F420 reduction by Frh is very rapid and most likely diffusion-limited (Livingston et al., 1987).
evidence: Stated as an inference from the rigidity of the complex, supported by citation

claim: F420 reduction by Frh is very rapid and most likely diffusion-limited.
source: This suggests that conformational changes do not play a role for the access of F420 to the hydride donor, consistent with the finding that F420 reduction by Frh is very rapid and most likely diffusion-limited (Livingston et al., 1987).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Direct electron detection cameras open new horizons for cryo-EM.
source: The advent of direct electron detection cameras opens new horizons for cryo-EM.
evidence: Stated as a general conclusion about the impact of the technology

claim: It is now possible to obtain higher-resolution maps with many fewer images using direct electron detectors.
source: It is now possible to obtain higher-resolution maps with many fewer images.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the advantages of direct electron detectors

claim: Using video data collection mode, the optimal data in terms of SNR or radiation damage can be extracted a posteriori.
source: Using the video data collection mode, the optimal data in terms of SNR or radiation damage can be extracted a posteriori
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the advantages of video mode

claim: Frame alignment schemes can be fine-tuned to the object under investigation.
source: and frame alignment schemes can be fine-tuned to the object under investigation.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion about the flexibility of video processing

claim: The purification of the Frh complex from Methanothermobacter marburgensis was performed as previously described.
source: The purification of the Frh complex from Methanothermobacter marburgensis and the preparation of the grids for the electron microscope data collection were performed as described (Mills et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a method with citation to previous work

claim: 3 μl of a 0.7 mg/ml Frh sample in the presence of 10 mM F420 was applied to Quantifoil R1/4 holey carbon grids.
source: Briefly, 3 μl of a 0.7 mg/ml Frh sample in the presence of 10 mM F420 was applied to freshly glow discharged Quantifoil R1/4 holey carbon grids (Quantifoil Micro Tools, Jena, Germany).
evidence: Stated as a method used in the study

claim: Data was collected on an FEI Tecnai Polara operating at 300 kV.
source: Data was collected on an FEI Tecnai Polara operating at 300 kV, using a back-thinned FEI Falcon II direct electron detector.
evidence: Stated as a method used in the study

claim: The calibrated magnification on the 14 µm pixel camera was 106,000, resulting in a 1.32 Å pixel size at the specimen.
source: The calibrated magnification on the 14 µm pixel camera was 106,000, resulting in a 1.32 Å pixel size at the specimen.
evidence: Stated as a method parameter

claim: Videos were collected for 1.5 s with a total of 24 frames with a calibrated dose of 3.5 e−/Å2 per frame.
source: Videos were collected for 1.5 s with a total of 24 frames with a calibrated dose of 3.5 e−/Å2 per frame, at various defocus values in the range between 0.8 and 3.8 μm.
evidence: Stated as a method parameter

claim: Tetrahedral symmetry was applied in all refinements.
source: Tetrahedral symmetry was applied in all refinements.
evidence: Stated as a method used in data processing

claim: B factors between −150 and −230 Å2 were found for all maps.
source: For all maps, B factors between −150 and −230 Å2 were found.
evidence: Stated as a result from post-processing

claim: The final model for the FrhABG heterotrimer contains 893 amino acid residues out of a possible 903.
source: The final model for the FrhABG heterotrimer contains 893 amino acid residues out of a possible 903, a [NiFe] cluster, four [4Fe4S] clusters, one FAD, and two metal ions, one of them coordinated by two trimers.
evidence: Stated as a description of the final model

claim: 96.5% of residues in the final model have backbone dihedral angles in the most favored region of the Ramachandran plot.
source: 96.5% of residues have backbone dihedral angles in the most favored region of the Ramachandran plot and the remaining 3.5% are in the generously allowed regions.
evidence: Stated as a validation metric for the final model

claim: Excluding glycine, aspartate and glutamate, 86% of side chains are well visible in the 3.36 Å map.
source: Excluding glycine, aspartate and glutamate, 86% of side chains are well visible.
evidence: Stated as a quantification of map quality, shown in Figure 9

claim: Unresolved side chains other than aspartate and glutamate are mostly located on the surface.
source: Unresolved side chains other than aspartate and glutamate are mostly located on the surface.
evidence: Stated as an observation about the distribution of unresolved side chains, shown in Figure 9

claim: Particles were clearly distinguishable below 1 μm defocus with a 1.5 s exposure (~90 e/Å2).
source: The particles were clearly distinguishable below 1 μm defocus with a 1.5 s exposure (∼90 e/Å2) (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated as an observation about data quality, shown in Figure 1A

claim: Thon rings are visible beyond 80% of the Nyquist frequency at 0.3 Å−1.
source: Thon rings are visible beyond 80% of the Nyquist frequency at 0.3 Å−1.
evidence: Stated as an observation about CTF quality, shown in Figure 1B
